status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should provide meaningful information making stakeholders aware of interactions with AI, including workplace interactions.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Section 1.3(ii) addresses information about interactions with AI. The victim consumed a static synthetic advertisement and then communicated with human scammers; no AI interlocutor is established. The false professional premise is an identity/provenance failure, without substituting that object for AI-interaction awareness.

review.reason_for_change: Section 1.3(ii) concerns information before or during interaction with AI. Victims viewed static advertisements and dealt with human scammers. No interaction with the generation system or autonomous AI interlocutor is established.

review.requirement_proposition: Protect vulnerable users, require specific consent for bounded deceptive styles, document emergent deception and define safeguard-failure protocols.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The Bronx account describes synthetic attorney impersonation, immigration-document disclosure and financial loss reported in August 2026. For IEEE-7014.1 6.7.3(l-p), the missing applicability fact is whether the operator adopted IEEE 7014.1 for an emulated-empathy GPAI partner in the interaction and the applicable vulnerable-user or deceptive-style safeguard context; impersonation imagery or task deception alone does not establish a human–AI partnering undertaking. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: 6.7.3(l-p) concerns emulated-empathy partner safeguards or emotional-data consent. Static advertisements and human-directed contact do not identify that object.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: ABC7 interviewed Hernandez and Leal. Leal denied authorising the identity clone, and Hernandez described sending money and sensitive documents in reliance on it. The requester’s AI-mediated impersonation did not respect privacy, dignity and autonomy. The result is Not aligned for this reported use. The other immigration-services case is contextual.

review.requirement_proposition: Add intended purpose, nominal operator and responsible contact information to the public documentation.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: IEEE 7001 Table 2 level 3 governs identification/public documentation of an autonomous system. The established recipient mechanism is a static generated advertisement and human-directed scam follow-up, not an autonomous participant. Synthetic likeness provenance is distinct from this autonomous-system transparency object.

review.reason_for_change: Table 2 level 3 concerns autonomous-system identification or public system documentation. A human-directed static advertisement and follow-up are not an established autonomous AI participant.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must ensure adequate transparency requirements tailored to the context and risk of AI lifecycle activities, including identification of AI-generated content.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 8 addresses Parties and their implemented territorial lifecycle duties. The US scam record does not establish entry into force for the relevant Party/territory or implementation covering these actors. No treaty finding is inferred from the attorney’s identity misuse.

review.reason_for_change: Article 8 concerns treaty Party implementation. No relevant commenced Party implementation duty is established for these US/Australian scammers or platforms.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not apply affective modeling to identifiable subject data without prior informed consent.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The Bronx account describes synthetic attorney impersonation, immigration-document disclosure and financial loss reported in August 2026. For IEEE-7014 4.3.5.2(d), the missing applicability fact is whether the developer undertook IEEE 7014 for an emulated-empathy system applying affective modelling to identifiable subject affective data; image depiction, face swapping or identity matching does not by itself establish affective modelling, and the anonymous-data exception cannot be resolved without that processing scope. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: 4.3.5.2(d) concerns affective modelling. Cloning a professional or public-figure likeness does not identify modelling that person’s emotions.

review.requirement_proposition: Make the system clearly identifiable as autonomous to users and bystanders.

review.reason_for_change: Table 2 level 1 concerns autonomous-system identification or public system documentation. A human-directed static advertisement and follow-up are not an established autonomous AI participant.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must seek to ensure that people interacting with AI are told they are interacting with a system rather than a human, as appropriate to the context.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not place, put into service or use AI that deploys subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques causing materially distorted behavior and significant harm.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The Bronx victim reports a $4,820 loss and document disclosure after an AI-generated advertisement impersonated an immigration attorney. The record does not identify the generating system or establish an EU-market provider, Union-established deployer, or output used in the Union. The serious reported deception is material, but the Article 2 territorial and actor connection is not established.

review.reason_for_change: Article 5(1)(a) requires covered territorial AI use and the defined manipulation/vulnerability harm conditions. The Bronx scam or Australian public-figure scam reports do not establish Union scope. No EU prohibition finding is inferred from fraud reports.

review.requirement_proposition: Minimise data and make review, modification and withdrawal of consent immediate and accessible.

review.reason_for_change: 6.22.3(a-b) concerns emulated-empathy partner safeguards or emotional-data consent. Static advertisements and human-directed contact do not identify that object.

review.reason_for_change: Article 5(1)(b) requires covered territorial AI use and the defined manipulation/vulnerability harm conditions. The Bronx scam or Australian public-figure scam reports do not establish Union scope. No EU prohibition finding is inferred from fraud reports.

review.requirement_proposition: Document interactions with GAI systems to users prior to interactive activities, particularly in contexts involving more significant risks.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: GV-5.1-002 addresses information to users before interactive GAI activities. The bounded recipient path was a static AI advertisement followed by human scammers’ demands; no interactive GAI participant is established. The attackers’ unpublished generation request is a separate activity and not substituted for the victim-facing route.

review.reason_for_change: GV-5.1-002 concerns information before or during interaction with AI. Victims viewed static advertisements and dealt with human scammers. No interaction with the generation system or autonomous AI interlocutor is established.

conclusion_change.previous: Human scammers used AI-generated advertising impersonating attorney Angel Leal to create a false professional relationship and economic service premise, inducing payment and sensitive-document disclosure. The requester-side use of Leal’s identifiable likeness lacked his authorization; this supports the identity-authority failure without identifying an internal generator control. The AI system’s independent tactic-selection objective remains unproved. Requester-side identity-bound cloning without the attorney’s authorization supports the neutral likeness-authority failure; identifying the generator is not mandatory. This is separate from the payment/disclosure and social-engineering failures and the still-ambiguous AI-side objective. Static advertisements and human-directed follow-up do not establish an autonomous interactive participant or named standards adoption.
conclusion_change.new: Human scammers used AI-generated advertising impersonating attorney Angel Leal to create a false professional relationship and economic service premise, inducing payment and sensitive-document disclosure. The requester-side use of Leal’s identifiable likeness lacked his authorization; this supports the identity-authority failure without identifying an internal generator control. The AI system’s independent tactic-selection objective remains unproved. Requester-side identity-bound cloning without the attorney’s authorization supports the neutral likeness-authority failure; identifying the generator is not mandatory. This is separate from the payment/disclosure and social-engineering failures and the still-ambiguous AI-side objective. Static advertisements and human-directed follow-up do not establish an autonomous interactive participant. The independent dignity and autonomy assessment is Not aligned for the reported impersonation. Generator-specific controls are not established.
